title: Kill a third of your backlog in 5 minutes, no spreadsheet
description:
Before you build a RICE spreadsheet, run the fastest prioritization framework there is: a value vs. effort 2x2. Plot every backlog item, then delete the entire low-value, high-effort quadrant with zero further analysis. In the lesson's worked example, a team drops 6 of 20 items that way and only RICE-scores what survives. Rough triage first, precision later.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/04-prioritization-basics/

#Shorts

beats.narration: You can kill a third of your backlog in five minutes, no spreadsheet. Here's the trick most teams skip.
When you need to prioritize fast, in a backlog grooming or a roadmap workshop, you skip the RICE spreadsheet and plot every item on a two by two. Value on one axis, effort on the other.

display.heading: The fastest framework
display.subheading: a first-pass 2x2, not a final call

beats.narration: That leaves four quadrants. High value, low effort are your quick wins. High value, high effort are major projects you plan deliberately.
A team finishes a discovery sprint with twenty backlog items. They sort all twenty into the quadrants, then throw out the low value, high effort pile, six items, without further analysis.
Those six were never getting built. The remaining fourteen go on to get RICE scored. Rough triage first, precision later.
The full breakdown of all three frameworks is in the lesson.
